1. $\theta^\top x$ is real-valued and unbounded; binary labels need outputs in (or decisions over) $\{0,1\}$.
2. $\sigma(t)=1/(1+e^{-t})$; range $(0,1)$.
3. $e^{v_j}/\sum_k e^{v_k}$.
4. $L=-\sum_k y_k\log([h_\theta(x)]_k)$.
5. Second-order methods need huge Hessians (size $\sim P^2$ for $P$ parameters) that cannot be inverted at modern scale.
